## Potential Code Enhancements

### Example: Improving the `SidenoteReact` Component

Ensure that the `SidenoteReact` component is optimized for performance and accessibility.

```jsx:src/components/SidenoteReact.tsx
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
import { subscribeToHighlight, setHighlightedNote, subscribeToVisibility } from './noteState';

interface SidenoteProps {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  number: number;
  id?: string;
}

export default function SidenoteReact({ children, number, id = `sn-${number}` }: SidenoteProps) {
  const [isMobile, setIsMobile] = useState(false);
  const [isHighlighted, setIsHighlighted] = useState(false);
  const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(true);
  const noteRef = useRef<HTMLSpanElement>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    // Handle responsiveness
    const handleResize = () => {
      setIsMobile(window.innerWidth <= 768);
    };
    window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize);
    handleResize();

    // Subscribe to highlight events
    const highlightSubscription = subscribeToHighlight(id, setIsHighlighted);
    const visibilitySubscription = subscribeToVisibility(id, setIsVisible);

    return () => {
      window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize);
      highlightSubscription.unsubscribe();
      visibilitySubscription.unsubscribe();
    };
  }, [id]);

  return (
    <>
      <span
        ref={noteRef}
        id={id}
        className={`sidenote ${isHighlighted ? 'highlighted' : ''}`}
        aria-label={`Sidenote ${number}`}
      >
        {number}. {children}
      </span>
    </>
  );
}
```

**Improvements Made:**

- **Accessibility**: Added `aria-label` for better screen reader support.
- **Performance**: Cleaned up event listeners to prevent memory leaks.
- **Responsiveness**: Enhanced the responsiveness handling within the component.

Let me analyze how themes are handled in both parts of your site:

## Main Site (phenomenal.ink)

The main site appears to use CSS variables for theming, defined in your global CSS. The theme toggle is managed through a React component that updates the `data-theme` attribute on the `html` element.

```tsx:src/components/ThemeToggle.tsx
export default function ThemeToggle() {
  // ... existing code ...
  const [theme, setTheme] = useState(() => {
    if (typeof localStorage !== 'undefined' && localStorage.getItem('theme')) {
      return localStorage.getItem('theme');
    }
    return 'light';
  });

  useEffect(() => {
    const root = document.documentElement;
    root.setAttribute('data-theme', theme);
    localStorage.setItem('theme', theme);
  }, [theme]);
  // ... rest of component ...
}
```

Your CSS variables are likely structured something like:

```css:src/styles/global.css
:root[data-theme="light"] {
  --background-color: #fffff8;
  --text-color: #111;
  --accent-color: #111;
  // ... other light theme variables ...
}

:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  --background-color: #111;
  --text-color: #fffff8;
  --accent-color: #fffff8;
  // ... other dark theme variables ...
}
```

## Blog Site (blog.phenomenal.ink)

The blog, using Starlight, handles themes differently. Starlight provides built-in theme support through its own system:

export const THEME_KEY = 'phenomenal-theme';

export function syncThemeAcrossSubdomains(newTheme: string) {
  // Set theme in localStorage
  localStorage.setItem(THEME_KEY, newTheme);
  
  // Broadcast theme change to other tabs/windows

}
